native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among the ever-incarcerated (n=289, jailed 1985-1994), 1985 composite wealth is compressed at the bottom of the distribution (pooled median $720, IQR $0-$6,000, 95% CI $0-$1,205; 39.4% report exactly zero wealth), and disparities within this group run along both race and sex. Race: ever-jailed white respondents have median $2,200 (n=69, IQR $0-$9,100, CI $400-$5,200) versus $320 for black respondents (n=159, IQR $0-$4,700, CI $0-$1,000) and a median of exactly $0 for Hispanic respondents (n=61, median on the zero tie block, so described qualitatively). That is roughly a seven-fold white-vs-black gap, but the median-difference CIs include zero (white-black -$1,880, CI -$5,004 to +$200; white-Hispanic -$2,200, CI -$5,000 to +$502), so the race disparity is stated most defensibly on zero-asset prevalence: 23.2% of ever-jailed white respondents hold zero wealth versus 43.4% of black (-20.2 pp, CI -32.9 to -7.9) and 47.5% of Hispanic (-24.4 pp, CI -40.2 to -8.5), while black and Hispanic are indistinguishable (-4.1 pp, CI -17.9 to +10.3). Sex: ever-jailed women are worse off than ever-jailed men - median $0 (n=37) versus $1,000 (n=252, CI $260-$1,480), difference -$1,000 (CI -$1,400 to -$259), driven by 64.9% of ever-jailed women holding zero wealth versus 35.7% of men (+29.2 pp, CI +12.5 to +45.4). The only race x sex contrasts with CIs excluding zero involve the small exploratory female cells ($0 for black female n=16 and Hispanic female n=9) versus white males ($2,000): -$2,000, CI -$5,200 to -$400. As supporting context, the ever-jailed hold far less than the never-jailed (crude median gap -$2,880, CI -$3,638 to -$2,298); reweighting to the ever-jailed race x sex distribution shrinks this to -$1,967 (CI -$2,742 to -$922), so about a third of the crude gap is compositional (the jailed group is 87% male and disproportionately black) and a large deficit remains. These are descriptive group differences in wealth measured at/around the start of the 1985-1994 incarceration window, not estimated consequences of incarceration; they are unweighted, unadjusted, and medians that sit on the zero tie block should be read as 'no assets' rather than as precise quantities.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Profiled data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows x 6 cols, no missing; ever_jailed=1 n=289). 2) Primary analysis: RAW composite_wealth_1985 within ever_jailed=1, by race, sex, race x sex, reporting n, median, IQR, mean, %exactly-zero, %negative, min/max, plus fixed-seed percentile bootstrap CIs (B=2,000, seed 20261023); pre-specified n<30 exploratory flag (black/female 16, white/female 12, hipanic/female 9) applied without suppression; tie-block rule flags cells whose median is 0 or whose zero tie block spans the cell's 25th-75th percentile, and those cells are described qualitatively. 3) Added a robust complement because medians are tie-bound: zero-asset / positive-asset prevalence within the jailed group with bootstrapped difference CIs in percentage points. 4) Context: same statistics for ever_jailed=0 and median gaps (bootstrapped), reported crude AND race x sex composition-standardised (distributional reweighting of cell medians using ever-jailed cell shares, not covariate adjustment). 5) Co-equal sensitivities: positive-values-only; winsorised at full-sample 1st/99th percentile (-5,063.36 / 273,949.04); de-duplication of 1,899 exact duplicate rows; explicit sign-flip table across measures. 6) Secondary/exploratory repeats for 1990 and 1996 wealth to test ordering stability over time. UNAVAILABLE ROUTES (recorded, not omitted): (a) inferring incarceration from residence in a detention facility -- the file exposes no residence/living-arrangement field; (b) adjustment for jail timing, duration or release, and all demographic or human-capital covariates -- none exposed. All estimates are unweighted, so they are neither design-based nor nationally representative; CIs describe sampling variability in this sample only, not survey standard errors. Race label 'hipanic' is a source misspelling retained in tables and glossed as Hispanic in prose.
